paragraphs.source_en: For the universe to continue to expand and new matter to be created, the steady state model required a modification of general, relativity, but the rate of creation needed was very low: about one particle per cubic kilometre per year, which would not conflict with observation. The theory also predicted that the average density of galaxies and similar objects should be constant both in space and time. However, a survey of sources of radio waves outside our galaxy, carried out by Martin Ryle and his group at Cambridge, showed that there were many more faint sources than strong ones. On average, one would expect the faint sources to be the more distant ones.
